items.note: Root cause unchanged: engine.js (sql-practice@1 adapter, outside this branch) still accepts a ragged multi-row VALUES, so Output still prints INSERT 0 2 for INSERT INTO students VALUES (7,...,'Hull'),(8,'Hana','hana@example.com'); where a server raises "VALUES lists must all be the same length". In-page mitigation verified in the simulator: the Activity 2 check no longer ticks "rows" and adds a true note ("PostgreSQL requires every row after VALUES to have the same number of values ... this practice editor did not stop it"). The misleading Output line remains until the adapter recipe lands.

The o1 distractor feedback now reads "VALUES appears only once in an INSERT; the second row goes after a comma, not after another VALUES", which is true and no longer claims the column list is missing.

The footer now says the practice editor imitates PostgreSQL's results and error wording and that its runs on this page were not repeated on a live PostgreSQL server; the unverified PostgreSQL 18 comparison claim is gone.

Reading column and Recap now say "An equality test on the primary key, such as course_id = 104" and "an equality test on every column of the primary key matches at most one row"; Activity 4 says "an equality test on both columns". True per 6.2 and 6.3.

Unchanged and accepted as an adapter recipe: execUpdate in engine.js still checks key uniqueness at the end of the statement (UPDATE instructors SET instructor_id = 5 - instructor_id; still prints UPDATE 4), and no LIMITS line was added. Low impact; no task on the page depends on it. Server outcome documented, not executed.
